timeline.author: Uri Baghin

timeline.body: The name is a bit of a mouthful, but it mirrors the existing `transitive_compile_time_jars`. I noticed it's also exposed as `transitive_deps`, maybe this should just be `transitive_full_deps`?
I can revert this if it's better to not have unrelated changes.

Note this doesn't add a way of specifying transitive full compile time jars explicitly when creating a new java provider through `JavaInfo` or `java_common.provider`.

I looked at the code a bit and it wasn't clear to me what the best semantics for that would be. Right now if you explicitly specify transitive jars it will set those, if you specify none it will get both them transitive jars and transitive full jars from the compiler args.
So maybe either both should be overridden or both inferred? Or maybe if you don't specify transitive full but specify transitive transitive full should default to transitive? Should it depend on the value of `useIjar`?
@uri-canva did you see my question in the bug?

No I didn't, I wasn't subscribed to that.

Sorry it turns out I didn't need this as my problem was due to a misunderstanding of how to use the datanucleus bytecode enhancer, the error messages were misleading and this changed fixed the problem I had, but it wasn't the correct way of fixing it.
